newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-RADKE WINS 16TH AS TWINS POUND BLUE JAYS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-RADKE WINS 16TH AS TWINS POUND BLUE JAYS.

text.p: Brad Radke won his 12th straight start to tie Rogers Clemens for the major league lead with 16 wins as the Minnesota Twins handed the reeling Toronto Blue Jays a 9-3 thumping on Monday.

Radke (16-5) allowed two unearned runs and five hits over seven innings to equal Scott Erickson's 1991 team record for consecutive victories. He walked three and struck out four in lowering his ERA to 3.34 while improving to 3-0 against Toronto this season.

"They hit a lot of balls hard and I got lucky tonight," said Radke. "I got away with a lot of pitches. A lot of mistake pitches they hit right to guys, but I'll take games like that. My guys are scoring runs and I'll take that too."
Greg Colbrunn provided the big blast for the Twins, coming off the bench in the fifth to hit a grand slam.

Leading 3-0, the Twins loaded the bases with one out. Omar Daal relieved starter Chris Carpenter (0-4) and Colbrunn, batting for Scott Stahoviak, greeted him by driving the second pitch over the wall in right for a 7-0 lead. It was Minnesota's first pinch homer of the season.
Carpenter was charged with six runs and eight hits in 4-1/3 innings for Toronto, losers of nine of its last 10.
In Kansas City, Charlie Hayes hit a pair of solo homers and Paul O'Neil homered and drove in two runs as the New York Yankees built a 5-0 lead and held on for a 5-4 victory over the Royals.

David Wells (12-5) flirted with his third shutout in four starts before the Royals scored four in the ninth, capped by Mike Sweeney's two-run homer off reliever Jeff Nelson. Mariano Rivera came on and picked up his league-leading 33rd save.
Wells ended up charged with three runs and six hits with a walk and six strikeouts in 8 1/3 innings. Glendon Rusch (3-8) yielded four runs and seven hits in six innings.
Hayes smacked a solo shot against Rusch in the fourth to give New York a 2-0 lead and went back-to-back with Paul O'Neill in the sixth to make it 4-0.
At Texas, Troy O' Leary ripped a bases-loaded triple as the Boston Red Sox rallied for seven runs over the final two innings to defeat the Rangers 11-5.

With the Red Sox trailing 5-4 in the eighth, Boston loaded the bases on singles by John Valentin and Wil Cordero and a walk to Mike Stanley. O'Leary then laced the first pitch he saw from reliever Danny Patterson (7-5) just out of right fielder Rusty Greer's reach to make it 7-5.
Boston added four more in the ninth with the help of a two-run triple by Jesus Tavarez.
In Detroit, Manny Ramirez homered and drove in four runs and Charles Nagy pitched seven strong innings to lead the Cleveland Indians to a 7-2 win over the Tigers.

Ramirez lofted a sacrifice fly in the top of the first to give the Indians a 1-0 lead. His 15th homer, a two-run shot in the third off starter Scott Sanders, extended the advantage to 4-1 and Ramirez added an RBI single in the ninth.
Jim Thome contributed his 30th homer for the Indians.

Nagy (11-7) allowed two runs and seven hits with three walks and seven strikeouts. Sanders (3-9), who fell to 0-3 since being acquired from Seattle last month, was tagged for five runs and eight hits in 4 2/3 innings.

In Anaheim, Scott Karl pitched six strong innings to win his fifth straight start and the Milwaukee Brewers hit three solo homers in the fourth inning as they defeated the Angels 5-2 for their 10th win in 12 games.
Karl (7-10) surrendered two runs -- one earned -- and five hits with no walks and six strikeouts.

The Brewers trailed 1-0 in the fourth before getting to Ken Hill (6-9). Jose Valentin led off with his 10th homer and, one out later, Dave Nilsson and Jeromy Burnitz hit back-to back solo shots for a 3-1 lead. An RBI single by Todd Dunn made it 4-1.
